title: Meet the LP-MSPM0L1306: what each part is for
credit: Board drawing: TI SLAU869E, leader lines removed

task_facts.head: What we ran on it
items: CoreMark 78.27 at 32 MHz, 2.45 per MHz: the same per-MHz score as the larger MSPM0G3507 chip at 32 MHz
Standard CoreMark with 144 bytes of RAM spare, Zephyr with our board files, an 8k-parameter AI model; not a 30k one
Only the UART loop test needs any (J16 and J17 to BP, one wire). Everything else runs on the board as shipped

label: USB and the debugger
Plug in here. The top half is a debugger
(XDS110): it loads your program onto the
chip and carries the chip's serial text
to your computer
J101: debugger to chip
Nine jumpers join the debugger to the chip:
power, serial, reset, programming. Leave
them on; take them off only to cut the
debugger off
S1 button (PA18)
A button your program can read. Held
while the board resets, it starts TI's
serial bootloader instead
Header pins J1 to J4
40 pins that fit BoosterPack plug-in
modules. Each pin's name is printed
beside it; 8 are not connected (NC)
Light sensor D1
A photodiode read through op-amp 0.
Jumpers J4, J5 and J6 connect it to
PA25, PA24 and PA22; take them off
to use those pins for your own parts
Thermistor RT1 (PA15)
Reads room temperature on ADC
channel 9. The two jumpers marked
T.PATH and T.PWR connect and power it
S3: reset
Restarts your program from the top
S2 button (PA14)
A second button, free for your program
J16 and J17: serial switch
Where serial pins PA8 and PA9 go.
XDS (right, as shipped): your computer.
BP (left): the header, for your own wires
The chip: MSPM0L1306
What you program: 32 MHz, 64 kB flash,
4 kB RAM. The RAM runs out first
LEDs
LED1 red on PA0, lit when the pin is low.
LED2 color: PA26 red, PA13 green,
PA27 blue. Jumpers J2, J3, J12 and J13
connect them
